title: Ribbe (Christmas Pork Belly with Crackling)
ingredients: 4 lbs (1.8 kg) pork belly, skin on, ribs attached
2 tbsp coarse sea salt, plus more for the skin
1 tbsp dark syrup or gravy browning (for color)
instructions: A day ahead, score the pork skin in a tight diamond pattern, cutting through the skin and fat but not into the meat.
Pat the skin completely dry, rub coarse salt and pepper into the scored skin and meat, and refrigerate uncovered overnight so the skin dries out.
The next day, pat the skin dry again, place the ribbe skin-side down in a roasting pan with about 1 cup of water, and roast at 300°F (150°C) for 2 to 2.5 hours.
Flip the ribbe skin-side up, increase the oven to 475°F (240°C), and roast for 15-25 minutes, watching closely, until the skin puffs up into crisp crackling (svor).
Remove and rest the meat for 15 minutes before carving between the ribs.
Skim the fat from the pan drippings, whisk in flour to make a roux, add stock and prunes, and simmer into a brown gravy (brun saus).
Serve with sauerkraut or braised red cabbage, boiled potatoes, and the brown gravy.

title: Pinnekjøtt (Steamed Salted Lamb Ribs)
ingredients: 4 lbs (1.8 kg) dried, salted lamb or mutton ribs (pinnekjøtt)
Birch sticks or a steaming rack
2 lbs (1 kg) rutabaga (swede), peeled and cubed
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Soak the dried, salted ribs in cold water for 24-36 hours, changing the water 2-3 times, to remove excess salt.
Arrange birch sticks (or a steaming rack) in the bottom of a large pot and add water just below the rack level.
Place the ribs on the sticks, bone-side down, cover tightly, and steam over low heat for 2.5-3 hours, topping up water as needed, until the meat is tender.
About 30 minutes before serving, boil the rutabaga until soft, then mash with butter, salt, and white pepper.
Boil the potatoes separately until tender.
Serve the steamed ribs with the mashed rutabaga, boiled potatoes, and a grinding of black pepper.

title: Fårikål (Mutton and Cabbage Stew)
ingredients: 2 lbs (1 kg) mutton or lamb shoulder, bone-in, cut into chunks
2 lbs (1 kg) cabbage, cut into wedges
2 lbs (1 kg) potatoes, boiled, to serve
instructions: In a large heavy pot, layer the meat and cabbage wedges alternately, starting and ending with cabbage.
Sprinkle whole peppercorns and salt between each layer.
Add the water, cover, and bring to a simmer.
Cook covered over low heat for 2 to 3 hours, until the meat is very tender, without stirring vigorously.
If a thicker broth is desired, whisk a little flour into some of the cooking liquid and stir back in, simmering a few more minutes.
Serve hot in bowls with boiled potatoes alongside.

title: Rakfisk (Fermented Trout)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs (700 g) rakfisk (fermented trout), thinly sliced or filleted
8 pieces thin potato flatbread (lefse) or flatbrød
instructions: Remove the rakfisk from its brine, rinse lightly, and pat dry.
Fillet and slice the fish thinly, leaving the skin on if desired.
Arrange the slices on a platter with the sliced red onion.
Serve with sour cream, boiled potatoes, melted butter, and chopped chives.
Eat by placing rakfisk, onion, and a spoonful of sour cream onto a piece of soft lefse or flatbrød and rolling or folding it up.
Traditionally served uncooked, accompanied by akevitt.

title: Lutefisk
ingredients: 1.5 cups dried green peas, soaked and cooked into a puree (ertestuing)
instructions: Salt the lutefisk lightly and let it sit for about an hour to firm the flesh, then rinse and pat dry.
Place the fish skin-side down in a baking dish, cover with foil, and bake at 450°F (230°C) for 20-30 minutes until just cooked through and gelatinous, not overcooked.
Alternatively, wrap loosely and poach gently in barely simmering water for about 20 minutes.
While the fish cooks, fry the bacon until crisp and warm the pea puree.
Boil the potatoes until tender.
Carefully drain the lutefisk of excess liquid and serve immediately with bacon, pea puree, boiled potatoes, melted butter, and mustard.

title: Klippfisk/Bacalao (Dried Salted Cod Stew)
ingredients: 2 lbs (1 kg) klippfisk (dried salted cod), soaked
2 lbs (1 kg) potatoes, peeled and sliced
instructions: Soak the klippfisk in cold water in the refrigerator for 24-48 hours, changing the water 3-4 times, until the salt is drawn out.
Drain, remove any skin and bones, and break the fish into large chunks.
In a large pot, sauté the onions, garlic, and bell peppers in olive oil until softened.
Add the crushed tomatoes, bay leaves, and chili, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the sliced potatoes and enough water to just cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Add the cod chunks and simmer gently for another 10-15 minutes until the fish is heated through and flaky.
Serve hot in bowls, drizzled with a little extra olive oil.

title: Kjøttkaker (Norwegian Meatballs in Brown Gravy)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs (700 g) ground beef and pork mix
instructions: In a bowl, whisk the flour into the milk until smooth, then mix in the egg, grated onion, allspice, salt, and pepper.
Add the ground meat and mix until well combined and slightly sticky.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into flattened, oval patties.
Fry the patties in butter over medium heat for 4-5 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Keep the patties warm and prepare or reheat the brown gravy, deglazing the frying pan with a little of it to capture the browned bits.
Serve the meatballs with the brown gravy, boiled potatoes, and lingonberry jam or stewed peas.

title: Lapskaus (Meat and Vegetable Stew)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs (700 g) beef chuck, cut into small cubes (or diced leftover roast)
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in a large pot, if using raw meat, then add the broth, bay leaf, and allspice.
Simmer covered for about 1.5 hours, until the meat is tender (skip this step and use pre-cooked leftover meat if preferred).
Add the onion, carrots, and rutabaga, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and continue simmering for another 15-20 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender and the stew has thickened slightly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot in bowls, traditionally with flatbread on the side.

title: Raspeballer (Potato Dumplings with Salted Meat)
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) boiled potatoes, peeled and cooled
1 lb (450 g) salted pork belly or bacon, in one piece plus extra slices
1 lb (450 g) smoked pork sausage (medisterpølse or similar)
instructions: Grate the raw potatoes finely, wrap in a cloth, and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Rice or mash the boiled potatoes and combine with the grated raw potato, flour, and salt to form a firm dough.
Shape the dough into fist-sized balls, tucking a small cube of salted pork into the center of each if desired.
Bring a large pot of salted water (or the water used to boil the salted pork) to a gentle simmer, and add the dumplings along with the piece of salted pork and sausage.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for 45-60 minutes, until the dumplings float and are cooked through.
Serve the dumplings whole or sliced, with the boiled salted pork, sausage, mashed rutabaga, and melted butter.

title: Fiskesuppe (Creamy Fish Soup)
ingredients: 1.5 lbs (700 g) firm white fish fillets (cod or haddock), cubed
1 small celeriac or 2 celery stalks, diced small
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot, add the carrot, leek, and celeriac, and sauté gently for 5 minutes without browning.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute to make a light roux.
Gradually whisk in the fish stock, bring to a simmer, and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream and return to a gentle simmer.
Add the cubed fish and shrimp, and poach gently for 5-6 minutes until just cooked through.
Season with salt and white pepper, and garnish with fresh dill before serving.

title: Fiskeboller (Fish Balls in White Sauce)
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) skinless white fish fillets (cod or haddock), very cold
instructions: In a food processor, blend the cold fish, egg white, potato starch, salt, and nutmeg until smooth.
With the processor running, slowly add the cold cream until the mixture is light and fluffy; chill for 30 minutes.
Using two spoons, shape the mixture into small ovals and poach gently in barely simmering salted water for 8-10 minutes until they float and firm up.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for a minute.
Gradually whisk in the fish stock or milk and simmer until smooth and thickened into a white sauce (hvit saus).
Drain the fish balls and serve napped with the white sauce, alongside boiled carrots and potatoes.

title: Sursild (Pickled Herring)
instructions: Soak the salted herring fillets in cold water for 12-24 hours, changing the water a few times, to remove excess salt.
Drain and cut the herring into bite-sized pieces.
In a saucepan, combine the vinegar, water, sugar, bay leaves, allspice, peppercorns, and mustard seeds, and bring to a boil to dissolve the sugar, then cool completely.
Layer the herring pieces and sliced red onion in a clean glass jar.
Pour the cooled pickling brine over the herring, ensuring it is fully submerged.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 24 hours, and up to a week, before serving cold.

title: Gravlaks (Dill-Cured Salmon)
ingredients: 2 lbs (1 kg) center-cut salmon fillet, skin on, pin bones removed
2 tbsp crushed white or black peppercorns
1 large bunch fresh dill, roughly chopped
2 tbsp Dijon mustard, for the sauce
1 tbsp white wine vinegar, for the sauce
0.33 cup neutral oil, for the sauce
instructions: Mix the salt, sugar, and crushed pepper together and rub evenly over both sides of the salmon.
Place half the dill in a dish, lay the salmon skin-side down on top, and cover with the remaining dill.
Wrap tightly in plastic wrap, place a weighted tray on top, and refrigerate for 24 to 72 hours, turning and basting with the accumulated liquid every 12 hours.
Scrape off the dill and cure, pat the salmon dry, and slice thinly on the diagonal away from the skin.
For the mustard sauce, whisk together the mustard, sugar, and vinegar, then slowly whisk in the oil until emulsified; stir in chopped dill.
Serve the sliced gravlaks with the mustard sauce and lefse or bread.

title: Rømmegrøt (Sour Cream Porridge)
ingredients: 2 tbsp sugar, mixed with 1 tsp cinnamon, for topping
instructions: Bring the sour cream to a gentle boil in a heavy-bottomed pot, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle in half the flour, whisking constantly, and continue cooking until the butterfat separates and rises to the surface; skim off and reserve this butter.
Whisk in the remaining flour to form a thick paste.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk, a little at a time, until the porridge reaches a smooth, pourable consistency.
Season with salt and simmer for a few more minutes, whisking, until thickened.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with the reserved butter (or melted butter), and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar; serve with cured meats on the side if desired.

title: Lefse (Soft Potato Flatbread)
ingredients: 1.5-2 cups flour, plus more for rolling
Extra butter and sugar, for serving
instructions: Boil the potatoes until very tender, then rice or mash them thoroughly with no lumps and let cool completely, preferably overnight in the refrigerator.
Work the butter, cream, and salt into the cold mashed potatoes, then gradually mix in the flour until a soft dough forms.
Divide into balls, and roll each one out very thinly on a floured surface into a large round.
Cook on a dry, hot griddle or lefse grill for 1-2 minutes per side, until lightly browned spots appear.
Stack the cooked lefse between clean kitchen towels to keep soft as they cool.
Serve folded with butter and a sprinkle of sugar or cinnamon sugar.

title: Krumkake
instructions: Whisk the eggs and sugar together until pale and slightly thickened.
Whisk in the melted butter and cream.
Fold in the flour, potato starch, and cardamom until a smooth batter forms.
Heat a krumkake iron and drop a small spoonful of batter in the center; close and cook for about 30-45 seconds per side until golden.
Working quickly while hot, remove the cookie and immediately roll it around a wooden krumkake cone.
Slide off once set and cool completely before storing; repeat with remaining batter.

title: Julekake (Christmas Fruit Bread)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and a pinch of sugar in the warm milk and let sit until foamy, about 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine flour, remaining sugar, cardamom, and salt, then work in the softened butter.
Add the yeast mixture and egg, and knead into a smooth, elastic dough, about 8-10 minutes.
Knead in the raisins and candied peel, then cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1.5 hours.
Shape into a round loaf, place on a lined baking sheet, and let rise again for 30-40 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 30-35 minutes until golden and cooked through; cool before slicing and serving with butter.

title: Vafler (Heart-Shaped Waffles)
ingredients: Butter, jam, or brown cheese (brunost), to serve
instructions: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, cardamom, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar, then whisk in the milk and sour cream.
Combine the wet and dry ingredients until just smooth, then whisk in the melted butter; let the batter rest for 20-30 minutes.
Heat a heart-shaped waffle iron and brush lightly with butter.
Ladle in batter and cook until golden and set, a bit softer than a Belgian waffle.
Serve warm topped with butter, sour cream and jam, or slices of brown cheese.

title: Smalahove (Salted Sheep's Head)
ingredients: 1 whole sheep's head, salted and smoked (prepared by a butcher)
2 lbs (1 kg) rutabaga (swede), peeled and cubed
instructions: Soak the salted, smoked sheep's head in cold water for several hours to overnight to draw out excess salt.
Place the head in a large pot, cover with fresh water, and simmer gently for 2.5-3 hours until the meat is tender and pulls easily from the bone.
About 30 minutes before the head is done, boil the rutabaga separately until soft, then mash with butter and season.
Boil the potatoes in a separate pot until tender.
Remove the head from the pot and let it rest briefly before serving whole or halved on a platter.
Serve with the mashed rutabaga, boiled potatoes, and black pepper, traditionally accompanied by akevitt.

title: Reinsdyrstek (Reindeer Steak with Cream Sauce)
ingredients: 2 lbs (1 kg) reindeer roast (loin or leg)
2 tbsp lingonberry jam, plus more to serve
instructions: Season the reindeer roast generously with salt, pepper, and crushed juniper berries.
Sear the roast on all sides in butter in a hot ovenproof pan until well browned.
Transfer to a 325°F (160°C) oven and roast until a meat thermometer reads 130-135°F (54-57°C) for medium-rare, then rest for 10-15 minutes.
Deglaze the searing pan with the stock, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer to reduce slightly.
Stir in the cream and lingonberry jam, and simmer until the sauce thickens lightly; season to taste.
Slice the roast thinly and serve with the cream sauce, boiled potatoes, and extra lingonberry jam.

title: Multekrem (Cloudberry Cream Dessert)
ingredients: 2 cups cloudberries (fresh or thawed frozen), plus extra whole berries for garnish
instructions: If using fresh cloudberries, gently mash about half of them with the sugar and set aside, keeping some whole for garnish.
Whip the cream with the vanilla until it holds soft peaks.
Gently fold the cloudberries and their juices into the whipped cream, being careful not to overmix so streaks of berry remain.
Taste and adjust sweetness if needed.
Spoon into serving glasses or bowls and garnish with whole cloudberries.
Chill briefly before serving.

title: Kransekake (Almond Ring Cake)
instructions: Mix the ground almonds and powdered sugar together in a large bowl.
Add the egg whites and almond extract, and knead into a smooth, firm marzipan-like dough; chill for at least an hour.
Roll the dough into ropes and press each into a greased ring mold (or shape freehand into rings of graduating sizes) from largest to smallest.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 10-12 minutes until just set and lightly golden; cool completely before removing from molds.
Whisk the icing egg white with powdered sugar and lemon juice until smooth and pipeable.
Stack the rings from largest at the base to smallest at the top, piping icing in zigzags between each layer to secure and decorate.

title: Riskrem (Rice Cream with Berry Sauce)
ingredients: 1 cup rice porridge (cooked short-grain rice pudding), chilled
instructions: For the berry sauce, simmer the berries with sugar and a splash of water until softened, then thicken with a cornstarch slurry and cool completely.
Whip the cream with sugar and vanilla until it holds firm peaks.
Gently fold the chilled rice porridge into the whipped cream until evenly combined and light.
Chill the riskrem for at least 1 hour.
Spoon into bowls or glasses.
Top generously with the cooled red berry sauce just before serving.

title: Pytt i Panne (Norwegian Hash)
ingredients: 2 cups diced cooked beef or leftover roast
Worcestershire sauce or ketchup, to serve
instructions: Melt half the butter in a large skillet and fry the diced potatoes over medium-high heat until golden and crisp, then set aside.
In the same skillet, fry the onion until softened, then add the diced meat and sausage and fry until browned and heated through.
Return the potatoes to the skillet, combine everything, and season with salt and pepper.
In a separate pan, fry the eggs sunny-side up in the remaining butter.
Divide the hash among plates and top each portion with a fried egg.
Serve with pickled beetroot and Worcestershire sauce or ketchup on the side.

title: Karbonader (Norwegian Meat Patties)
ingredients: 2 cups brown gravy (brun saus), to serve
instructions: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for a few minutes until softened.
Combine the soaked breadcrumbs with the ground beef, grated onion, egg, allspice, salt, and pepper, mixing just until combined.
Shape the mixture into flat, round patties about 0.75 inch thick.
Fry the patties in butter over medium heat for 4-5 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Keep warm while preparing or reheating the brown gravy.
Serve the patties with brown gravy, boiled potatoes, and stewed cabbage or lingonberry jam.

title: Torsketunger (Fried Cod Tongues)
instructions: Rinse the cod tongues and pat dry, then season with salt and pepper
Set up a dredging station with flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs in separate bowls
Coat each tongue first in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere
Melt butter in a heavy skillet over medium heat
Fry the tongues in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp
Drain briefly on paper towel and season with a little extra salt
Serve hot with lemon wedges, chopped parsley, and remoulade sauce alongside boiled potatoes

title: Pytt i Panne
ingredients: 300g cooked roast beef or leftover meat, diced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt half the butter in a large heavy skillet over medium heat and add the diced potatoes
Fry the potatoes, turning occasionally, for about 15 minutes until golden and tender
Push the potatoes to one side, add remaining butter and the onion, and fry until softened
Add the diced meat and mix everything together, frying for another 5-8 minutes until heated through and lightly crisped
Season generously with salt and pepper
In a separate pan, fry the eggs sunny-side up
Divide the hash between plates, top each with a fried egg, and serve with pickled beetroot

title: Kjøttsuppe (Norwegian Meat and Vegetable Soup)
ingredients: 1.5 lb (700g) bone-in beef or lamb, cut into chunks
instructions: Place the meat in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam
Add the peppercorns and salt, then reduce heat and simmer, covered, for about 1.5 hours until the meat is tender
Add the carrots, swede, and celeriac, and simmer for another 20 minutes
Add the potatoes and leek, and continue simmering for 15-20 minutes until all vegetables are tender
Stir in the marjoram and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper
Ladle the soup with meat and vegetables into bowls and garnish with fresh parsley

title: Spekeskinke (Norwegian Cured Ham)
ingredients: 1 fresh pork leg or shank (about 1.5 kg), bone-in
instructions: Mix the salt, sugar, crushed juniper berries, crushed peppercorns, and crumbled bay leaves together
Rub the mixture thoroughly over the entire pork leg, working it into every surface
Place the meat in a non-reactive container, cover, and refrigerate for 2-3 weeks, turning and basting with the brine that forms every few days
Rinse the cured meat well, pat dry, and hang in a cool, airy place for 2-3 months to dry-cure until firm
To serve, slice the finished spekeskinke paper-thin using a sharp knife or meat slicer
Arrange the slices on a platter with crusty bread, butter, and pickles

title: Fenalår (Cured Leg of Lamb)
instructions: Rub the leg of lamb all over with a mixture of coarse salt, sugar, and crushed peppercorns
Place in a container, cover, and cure in the refrigerator for about 3 weeks, turning occasionally and pouring off excess liquid
Rinse off the salt mixture, pat the leg dry, and hang it in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place for 4-6 months until firm and deep red throughout
When ready to serve, slice the fenalår very thinly against the grain
Arrange the slices on flatbread with a dollop of sour cream
Serve as a starter or part of a cold buffet (koldtbord)

title: Torskerogn (Poached Cod Roe)
ingredients: 1 lb (450g) fresh cod roe, in the membrane sac
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer with the salt and vinegar
Carefully lower the whole cod roe sac into the water and poach gently for 20-25 minutes until firm, without letting it boil hard
Remove and let cool slightly, then slice into rounds
Melt the butter in a skillet and fry the roe slices for 1-2 minutes per side until lightly golden
Serve warm with boiled potatoes, melted butter drizzled over, chopped chives, and black pepper

title: Tilslørte Bondepiker (Veiled Farm Girls)
ingredients: Red currant jelly, optional, for garnish
instructions: Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and add the breadcrumbs, sugar, and cinnamon
Toast, stirring constantly, until the crumbs are golden and fragrant, about 5 minutes, then let cool
In serving glasses or a large glass bowl, layer the spiced breadcrumbs and applesauce, starting and ending with breadcrumbs
Repeat the layers to fill the glasses
Top each serving with a generous dollop of whipped cream
Garnish with a small spoonful of red currant jelly if desired and serve chilled

title: Eplekake (Norwegian Apple Cake)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a springform or baking dish
Whisk together the eggs and 3/4 cup of the sugar until pale and fluffy
Stir in the melted butter, milk, and vanilla sugar, then fold in the flour and baking powder to form a smooth batter
Pour the batter into the prepared dish and arrange the apple slices on top in a decorative pattern
Mix the remaining sugar with the cinnamon and sprinkle over the apples, then scatter with sliced almonds
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden and a skewer inserted in the cake comes out clean
Cool slightly before slicing and serve with lightly whipped cream

title: Bløtkake (Norwegian Cream Layer Cake)
ingredients: Marzipan or chocolate shavings, for decoration
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease and line a round cake tin
Whisk the eggs and sugar together until very light, thick, and tripled in volume
Gently fold in the sifted flour and baking powder in batches, being careful not to deflate the batter
Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 30-35 minutes until springy to the touch, then cool completely and slice horizontally into three layers
Spread jam and a layer of whipped cream over the first layer, add sliced strawberries, and repeat with the second layer
Top with the final cake layer and cover the entire cake with the remaining whipped cream
Decorate the top with strawberries and marzipan or chocolate shavings, then chill for at least 1 hour before serving

title: Vossakorv (Smoked Sausage from Voss)
instructions: In a large bowl, mix the ground beef and pork with caraway, allspice, salt, and pepper until well combined
Stuff the seasoned meat mixture into the sausage casings, twisting into links about 15cm long
Cold-smoke the sausages over alder or birch wood for several hours if equipment is available, or simmer gently for a fresh version
To cook, prick the sausages and simmer in barely bubbling water for about 20 minutes, or pan-fry until browned and cooked through
Scramble the eggs in a separate pan
Slice the sausage and serve hot with scrambled eggs and flatbread

title: Rundstykker (Norwegian Breakfast Rolls)
ingredients: 25g fresh yeast (or 2 tsp active dry yeast)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk with the sugar
In a large bowl, combine the flour and salt, then add the milk mixture and softened butter, mixing to form a soft dough
Knead the dough for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled
Punch down the dough and divide into 8-10 equal pieces, shaping each into a round roll
Place the rolls on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise for another 30 minutes
Brush the tops with beaten egg and bake at 220°C (425°F) for 12-15 minutes until golden brown
Cool slightly on a wire rack and serve fresh with butter, brown cheese, or jam

title: Skillingsboller (Norwegian Cinnamon Buns)
ingredients: 100g butter, softened, plus extra for filling
2 tbsp ground cinnamon mixed with sugar, for filling
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk, then stir in sugar, cardamom, and salt
Add the flour and softened butter and knead into a smooth, elastic dough, about 10 minutes
Cover and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled in size
Roll the dough out into a large rectangle, spread with softened butter, and sprinkle generously with the cinnamon-sugar mixture
Roll up tightly into a log and cut into thick slices, placing them cut-side up in paper cups or on a baking sheet
Let rise again for 30 minutes, then brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with pearl sugar
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 12-15 minutes until deep golden brown, then cool on a wire rack

title: Rabarbragrøt (Rhubarb Pudding)
ingredients: Cold milk or cream, for serving
instructions: Combine the rhubarb and water in a pot and bring to a boil
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until the rhubarb has completely broken down and softened
Strain through a sieve for a smoother texture, or leave chunky, then return to the pot and stir in the sugar and vanilla sugar
Mix the potato starch with the cold water to form a smooth slurry
Bring the rhubarb mixture back to a gentle boil and stir in the slurry, cooking for 1-2 minutes until thickened and glossy
Pour into bowls and chill, or serve slightly warm, with cold milk or cream poured over the top

title: Blodpudding (Norwegian Blood Pudding)
ingredients: 1 liter fresh pig's or sheep's blood, strained
200g all-purpose flour, or a mix of flour and barley flour
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the blood with the milk until smooth
Gradually whisk in the flour, salt, allspice, and ginger to form a smooth, lump-free batter
Stir in the raisins and diced pork fat
Pour the mixture into greased loaf tins or baking dishes
Bake at 160°C (325°F) in a water bath for about 1 hour, until set and firm
Cool, then slice, and pan-fry the slices in butter until crisp on the outside
Serve warm with lingonberry jam and bacon

title: Blodklubb (Blood Dumplings)
ingredients: 400g grated raw potato, liquid squeezed out
instructions: Combine the strained blood with the grated potato in a large bowl
Stir in the flour and salt to form a thick, cohesive dough
Fold in the diced pork or bacon
Shape the mixture into round dumplings about the size of a fist
Lower the dumplings gently into a large pot of simmering, salted water and cook for 45-60 minutes until firm and cooked through
Remove with a slotted spoon, slice thickly, and pan-fry in butter until golden
Serve hot with melted butter and lingonberry jam

title: Fiskekaker (Norwegian Fish Cakes)
ingredients: 500g white fish fillets (cod or haddock), skinned and boned
instructions: Process the fish in a food processor until smooth, or finely mince by hand
Add the potato starch, egg, and salt, and process again until well combined
With the processor running, gradually add the milk to form a smooth, light batter
Stir in the grated onion and white pepper
Using two spoons, shape the mixture into oval patties
Fry the fish cakes in butter over medium heat for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through
Serve with boiled potatoes, melted butter, and creamed cabbage or a squeeze of lemon

title: Akevittsild (Aquavit-Cured Herring)
ingredients: 500g salted herring fillets, soaked and desalted
instructions: Rinse the desalted herring fillets and cut into bite-sized pieces
In a saucepan, combine the vinegar, sugar, allspice, and bay leaves, bring to a boil, then remove from heat and cool completely
Stir the aquavit into the cooled brine
Layer the herring pieces with the sliced onion and carrot in a clean glass jar
Pour the aquavit brine over to fully cover the herring
Seal and refrigerate for at least 24 hours, and up to a week, before serving
Garnish with fresh dill and serve with boiled potatoes and flatbread

title: Vafler med Brunost (Waffles with Brown Cheese)
ingredients: Brunost (Norwegian brown cheese), thinly sliced, for serving
instructions: Whisk the eggs and sugar together until light and slightly foamy
Whisk in half of the milk, then add the flour, baking powder, and cardamom, whisking until smooth
Whisk in the remaining milk and the melted butter to make a thin, pourable batter
Let the batter rest for 20-30 minutes
Heat a heart-shaped waffle iron and cook the waffles until golden brown and crisp
Serve the warm waffles immediately, topped with thin slices of brunost that melt slightly on contact, and a spoonful of jam if desired

title: Ribberull (Rolled Meat Roll)
ingredients: 1.5 kg flank of pork or veal, boned and flattened
instructions: Lay the flattened meat out flat, skin-side down, and season generously with salt, pepper, and allspice
Scatter the chopped parsley and onion evenly over the meat
Roll the meat up tightly into a log and tie securely at intervals with kitchen string
Place the roll in a pot, cover with water, and bring to a gentle simmer
Simmer for about 2 hours until fully cooked and tender, or roast in the oven at 160°C (325°F) until an internal temperature of 75°C is reached
Let cool completely, then wrap tightly and refrigerate under light weight overnight to compress
Slice thinly and serve cold as part of a Christmas cold cuts platter

title: Torskemiddag (Poached Cod Dinner)
ingredients: Cod liver and roe, boiled, optional, for serving
instructions: Bring the water to a gentle simmer with the salt in a wide, shallow pan
Lower the cod fillets into the barely simmering water, making sure they are fully submerged
Poach gently for 8-10 minutes, without letting the water boil, until the fish flakes easily
Meanwhile, melt the butter slowly until it turns a light nutty brown, or simply melt it and keep warm
Carefully lift the cod out with a slotted spatula and drain briefly
Serve the poached cod with boiled potatoes and carrots, generously drizzled with the melted butter and chopped dill

title: Rekesalat (Norwegian Shrimp Salad)
ingredients: Salt and white pepper, to taste
Toasted bread or crispbread, for serving
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, sour cream, and lemon juice
Gently fold in the shrimp, diced apple, and most of the chopped dill
Season to taste with salt and white pepper
Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors meld
Arrange lettuce leaves on plates or bread slices and spoon the shrimp salad on top
Garnish with the remaining dill and serve immediately

title: Lammelår (Norwegian Roast Leg of Lamb)
ingredients: 300ml water or stock, for the pan
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F)
Make small incisions all over the lamb and insert the garlic slivers, then rub the whole leg with rosemary, salt, pepper, and oil
Place the lamb on a bed of carrots and onion in a roasting pan and pour the water around it
Roast for 20 minutes at high heat, then reduce the oven temperature to 160°C (325°F) and continue roasting for about 1.5 hours, basting occasionally, until the internal temperature reaches 65-70°C
Remove the lamb, tent with foil, and let rest for 15-20 minutes
Strain the pan juices into a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and simmer to make a gravy, seasoning to taste
Carve the lamb and serve with the gravy, roasted vegetables, and boiled potatoes

title: Fiskepudding (Norwegian Fish Pudding)
ingredients: 500g white fish fillets (cod, haddock, or pollock), skinned and boned
Melted butter or shrimp sauce, for serving
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and generously butter a loaf tin or pudding mold
Puree the fish in a food processor until completely smooth
Add the potato starch, eggs, salt, and nutmeg, and process again to combine
With the machine running, slowly pour in the cream and milk until the batter is light and airy
Pour the batter into the prepared mold, cover with foil, and bake in a water bath for about 45-50 minutes until set and a skewer comes out clean
Let rest for 5 minutes, then unmold and slice
Serve warm with melted butter or a creamy shrimp sauce and boiled potatoes

title: Medisterkaker (Norwegian Spiced Pork Patties)
ingredients: 500g ground pork, preferably with some fat
instructions: In a bowl, mix the ground pork with salt, ginger, and allspice until well combined
Sprinkle in the potato starch and mix again
Gradually work in the cold milk a little at a time, beating the mixture until light and slightly fluffy
Stir in the grated onion
Shape the mixture into small, flat patties with wet hands
Fry the patties in butter over medium heat for about 5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through
Serve with sautéed cabbage, boiled potatoes, and brown gravy

title: Ertesuppe (Norwegian Split Pea Soup)
ingredients: 1 smoked ham hock or bacon knuckle
instructions: Rinse the split peas and soak in cold water for a few hours if time allows, then drain
Place the peas, water, and ham hock in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam
Reduce heat and simmer, partially covered, for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking
Add the carrots, leek, and onion, and continue simmering for another 30-40 minutes until the peas have broken down and the soup is thick
Remove the ham hock, shred the meat, and return it to the pot, discarding the bone and skin
Season with thyme, salt, and pepper to taste
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with a dollop of Norwegian mustard and flatbread on the side

title: Köttbullar (Swedish Meatballs in Cream Sauce with Lingonberry)
ingredients: 1 tsp soy sauce (for color and depth)
instructions: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 10 minutes to make a panade.
In a bowl, combine the ground beef, ground pork, minced onion, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, allspice, white pepper, and salt. Mix gently until just combined; do not overwork.
Wet your hands and roll the mixture into small, tight meatballs about 1 inch in diameter.
Melt half the butter in a skillet over medium heat and fry the meatballs in batches, shaking the pan to keep them round, until browned on all sides and cooked through. Set aside.
In the same skillet, melt the remaining butter and whisk in the flour to form a roux; cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and cream, simmering until the sauce thickens. Stir in the soy sauce for color.
Return the meatballs to the sauce and simmer gently for 5 minutes to warm through.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes and a spoonful of lingonberry preserves on the side.

title: Gravlax (Dill-Cured Salmon)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb fresh salmon fillet, skin-on, center cut, pin bones removed
1 large bunch fresh dill, roughly chopped
instructions: Mix the coarse salt, sugar, and crushed white peppercorns in a bowl.
Pat the salmon dry and place skin-side down on a large sheet of plastic wrap. Rub the salt mixture evenly over the flesh, then splash with the aquavit if using.
Pile the chopped dill on top of the fillet, pressing it into the flesh.
Wrap the salmon tightly in the plastic wrap and place it in a dish. Set a weighted plate or board on top to press it down.
Refrigerate for 48 to 72 hours, turning the parcel over and basting with the accumulated liquid every 12 hours.
To serve, scrape off most of the dill and cure, then slice the salmon thinly on the diagonal away from the skin.
Whisk together the mustard, vinegar, and sugar for the sauce, then slowly whisk in the oil until emulsified; stir in the chopped dill.
Serve the gravlax with the mustard-dill sauce and boiled potatoes or crisp bread.

title: Jansson's Frestelse (Jansson's Temptation)
ingredients: 2 lb starchy potatoes (such as Yukon Gold), peeled
2 tins (about 4 oz each) Swedish sprats or anchovy fillets in brine, with their liquid
3 tbsp butter, plus extra for dotting
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Butter a baking dish.
Cut the peeled potatoes into thin matchsticks (julienne).
Melt the butter in a pan and sauté the sliced onions until soft and translucent but not browned.
Layer half the potatoes in the baking dish, then all the onions and sprats with their brine, then top with the remaining potatoes. Season lightly with white pepper.
Pour the milk over the dish, then dot the surface with butter and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Bake uncovered for 30 minutes, then pour the cream evenly over the top.
Continue baking for another 20 to 30 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden and bubbling.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Ärtsoppa (Yellow Pea Soup with Pork)
ingredients: 1 lb dried yellow split peas, soaked overnight and drained
1 lb salted pork shoulder or lightly smoked pork knuckle
1 yellow onion, studded with 2 whole cloves
6 cups water, plus more as needed
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Place the soaked peas, pork, clove-studded onion, carrots, bay leaf, and thyme in a large pot and cover with the water.
Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam that rises to the surface.
Reduce heat and simmer gently, partially covered, for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the peas have broken down and the pork is tender.
Remove the pork, cut it into bite-sized pieces, and discard the onion and bay leaf.
Return the pork to the pot, stir well, and season with salt and white pepper to taste.
If the soup is too thick, thin with a little hot water; simmer 5 more minutes.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with a dab of Swedish mustard, traditionally on Thursdays.

title: Pytt i Panna (Swedish Hash)
ingredients: 1 lb boiled or leftover potatoes, diced small
1/2 lb leftover roast beef or ham, diced small
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Melt half the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and fry the diced onion until soft and lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining butter to the skillet and fry the diced potatoes in a single layer, turning occasionally, until crisp and golden on several sides.
Add the diced meat and cooked onion back to the skillet and fry together for a few more minutes until the meat is heated through and lightly crisped.
Season with salt and black pepper.
In a separate pan, fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Divide the hash among plates, top each with a fried egg, and serve with pickled beets and lingonberry preserves.

title: Raggmunk (Potato Pancakes with Fried Pork and Lingonberry)
ingredients: 1/2 lb thick-cut bacon or fatty salt pork slices
instructions: Fry the bacon or salt pork slices in a skillet until crisp; keep warm and reserve the rendered fat.
Whisk together the milk, flour, eggs, and salt to form a smooth, thin batter.
Coarsely grate the raw potatoes and fold them into the batter immediately to prevent discoloration.
Heat butter (and a little of the reserved bacon fat) in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Ladle the potato batter into the skillet to form thin pancakes, flattening slightly, and fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crisp at the edges.
Keep finished pancakes warm while frying the rest, adding more butter as needed.
Serve the raggmunk hot, stacked with the fried pork alongside and topped with lingonberry preserves.

title: Kroppkakor (Potato Dumplings Filled with Pork)
ingredients: 2 lb starchy potatoes, boiled, cooled, and riced
1/2 lb ground pork or finely diced fatty bacon
instructions: For the filling, sauté the chopped onion in a little butter until soft, then mix with the ground pork, allspice, salt, and pepper. Cook briefly to combine, then cool.
For the dough, combine the riced cold potatoes with the potato starch, egg, and salt, mixing just until a smooth dough forms.
Divide the dough into balls about the size of a fist. Flatten each into a disc in your palm.
Place a spoonful of the pork filling in the center of each disc, then fold the dough around it and roll gently into a smooth ball, sealing completely.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer (not a rolling boil) and carefully lower in the dumplings.
Simmer for about 20 minutes, until the dumplings float and are cooked through.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain well, and serve topped with melted butter and lingonberry preserves.

title: Smörgåstårta (Swedish Sandwich Cake)
ingredients: 8 slices soft white sandwich bread, crusts removed
1 cup heavy cream, whipped to stiff peaks (for frosting)
Lemon slices and extra shrimp, for garnish
instructions: Whip the cream cheese with half the mayonnaise until smooth and spreadable; divide into portions for each filling layer.
Lay a layer of bread slices side by side to form the base of the cake on a serving platter.
Spread with a layer of cream cheese mixture, then top with smoked salmon and a few cucumber slices; cover with a second layer of bread.
Spread again with cream cheese mixture, then top with chopped shrimp mixed with a little mayonnaise and sliced egg; cover with a final layer of bread.
Frost the entire outside of the cake (top and sides) with the whipped cream as you would a layer cake, smoothing it evenly.
Decorate the top with dill sprigs, lemon slices, and whole shrimp.
Chill for at least 1 hour before slicing and serving to let the layers set.

title: Räksmörgås (Open-Faced Shrimp Sandwich)
ingredients: 4 slices rustic white bread or crispbread
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: Butter each slice of bread generously all the way to the edges.
Place a lettuce leaf on each slice of buttered bread as a base layer.
Toss the shrimp gently with a spoonful of the mayonnaise, just enough to coat lightly, and season with salt and white pepper.
Arrange overlapping cucumber slices on the lettuce, then pile the shrimp generously on top.
Tuck slices of hard-boiled egg around the shrimp and add a dollop of the remaining mayonnaise.
Garnish with fresh dill sprigs and a lemon wedge on the side.
Serve open-faced immediately with a knife and fork.

title: Kalops (Swedish Beef Stew with Allspice)
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into large cubes
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Boiled potatoes and pickled beets, to serve
instructions: Pat the beef cubes dry and season with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a heavy pot or Dutch oven and brown the beef in batches over high heat; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the sliced onions until softened and lightly golden.
Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir to coat, cooking for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pot along with the carrots, bay leaves, allspice berries, and tomato paste if using. Pour in the beef stock and stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat (or in a 325°F/160°C oven) for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is fork-tender.
Remove the bay leaves, adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, and let the stew rest for a few minutes.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes and pickled beets.

title: Kåldolmar (Swedish Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: 1 lb ground beef and pork mix
2 tbsp golden syrup or light corn syrup
instructions: Core the cabbage and blanch the whole head in boiling salted water for a few minutes, peeling off softened outer leaves as they loosen; trim the thick center rib from each leaf.
Mix the ground meat, cooked rice, chopped onion, egg, milk, salt, and white pepper until well combined.
Place a spoonful of filling near the base of each cabbage leaf, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly into a neat parcel.
Melt half the butter in a large skillet or braising pan and brown the cabbage rolls on all sides.
Drizzle the syrup over the rolls and let it caramelize slightly, then pour in the beef stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 to 40 minutes, until the cabbage is tender and the filling is cooked through, basting occasionally with the pan juices.
Serve hot with the pan sauce and a spoonful of lingonberry preserves.

title: Inlagd Sill (Pickled Herring)
ingredients: 4 salted herring fillets (or matjes herring), soaked in cold water 12 to 24 hours if very salty
1 cup white vinegar (12%, diluted per instructions, or use standard 5% vinegar)
instructions: Drain the soaked herring fillets and pat dry, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
In a saucepan, combine the vinegar, sugar, and water and heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely; let the brine cool fully.
Layer the herring pieces with the sliced onion and carrot in a clean glass jar.
Add the allspice berries, peppercorns, and bay leaves to the jar.
Pour the cooled brine over the herring, making sure everything is fully submerged.
Seal the jar and refrigerate for at least 24 to 48 hours before serving to let the flavors develop.
Serve chilled, sprinkled with fresh dill, alongside boiled potatoes and crispbread.

title: Toast Skagen (Shrimp Toast)
ingredients: 1 lb small cooked, peeled shrimp, roughly chopped
2 tbsp crème fraîche or sour cream
1 tbsp lemon juice, plus lemon wedges to serve
A small spoonful of Swedish trout roe (löjrom), for garnish
Salt and white pepper, to taste
instructions: In a bowl, combine the chopped shrimp, mayonnaise, crème fraîche, dill, lemon juice, and red onion. Season with salt and white pepper and mix gently.
Chill the shrimp mixture for at least 15 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Trim the crusts from the bread slices, if desired, and cut each slice in half or into rounds.
Melt the butter in a skillet and fry the bread on both sides until golden and crisp.
Pile the chilled shrimp mixture generously onto each piece of toast.
Top each with a small spoonful of trout roe and an extra sprig of dill.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Falukorv med Makaroner (Falukorv with Macaroni)
ingredients: 1 lb falukorv sausage, scored and sliced into half-moons
8 oz macaroni or other short pasta
2 tbsp ketchup, plus more to serve
Chopped chives or parsley, for garnish
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the macaroni according to package directions until al dente; drain.
While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and fry the sliced onion, if using, until softened.
Add the sliced falukorv to the skillet and fry, turning occasionally, until browned and lightly crisped at the edges, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir the ketchup and mustard into the skillet with the sausage, tossing to coat evenly, and warm through.
Toss the drained macaroni directly into the skillet with the sausage, or plate the macaroni and top with the fried sausage.
Season with a little salt if needed and garnish with chopped chives or parsley.
Serve hot with extra ketchup on the side.

title: Sjömansbiff (Swedish Sailor's Beef and Potato Casserole)
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb beef chuck or sirloin, thinly sliced
2 lb potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Melt half the butter in a skillet and brown the sliced beef quickly in batches over high heat; season with salt and pepper and set aside.
In the same skillet, melt the remaining butter and sauté the sliced onions until soft and golden.
Whisk the flour into the onions, cook briefly, then gradually whisk in the beef stock, beer, and tomato paste to form a smooth sauce; add the bay leaf.
In a buttered casserole dish, layer half the sliced potatoes, then the browned beef and onions, then the remaining potatoes.
Pour the sauce evenly over the layers so the potatoes are mostly submerged.
Cover and bake for 1 to 1 1/4 hours, until the potatoes are tender, removing the cover for the last 15 minutes to brown the top.
Remove the bay leaf, garnish with chopped parsley, and serve hot directly from the dish.

title: Biff Rydberg
ingredients: 500g potatoes, peeled and diced into small cubes
3 tbsp butter, plus extra for frying
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Parboil the diced potatoes in salted water for about 4 minutes until just tender but still firm, then drain and pat dry.
Heat butter and oil in a frying pan and fry the potato cubes over medium-high heat until golden and crisp on all sides. Remove and set aside, keeping warm.
In the same pan, add a little more butter and fry the diced onions slowly until soft and golden, then remove and set aside.
Increase heat, add more butter to the pan, and sear the beef cubes quickly on all sides so they are browned outside but rare inside. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange the beef, potatoes, and onions in three separate mounds on each plate, keeping them distinct rather than mixed together.
Place a raw egg yolk in a small half eggshell or a small dish on top of each portion.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve immediately, with the diner stirring the egg yolk into the hot beef and potatoes at the table.

title: Pannkakor (Swedish Pancakes)
ingredients: 2 tbsp melted butter, plus extra for frying
instructions: Whisk the eggs with a little of the milk in a large bowl.
Add the flour, salt, and sugar, whisking until you have a smooth, lump-free batter.
Gradually whisk in the remaining milk until the batter is thin, similar to heavy cream, then stir in the melted butter.
Let the batter rest for 20-30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat a small amount of butter in a wide, flat frying pan over medium heat and pour in a thin layer of batter, tilting the pan to coat evenly.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until the edges lift and the underside is golden, then flip and cook briefly on the other side.
Stack the finished pancakes on a warm plate and repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve warm, rolled or folded, with lingonberry jam and whipped cream.

title: Semla
ingredients: 50g fresh yeast (or 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast)
2-3 tbsp milk (to soften the almond paste)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk in a large bowl, then add sugar, cardamom, salt, egg, and half the flour, mixing to combine.
Add the softened butter and remaining flour, then knead until you have a smooth, elastic dough. Cover and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch down the dough, divide into 10-12 pieces, and roll into round buns. Place on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise for another 45 minutes.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 8-10 minutes until golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Slice the top off each bun and scoop out a bit of the soft crumb from the center, reserving it.
Crumble the reserved bread with the almond paste and a splash of milk to form a soft filling, then spoon it into the hollowed buns.
Pipe generous whipped cream on top of the almond filling, then replace the bun lid and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Kanelbullar (Swedish Cinnamon Buns)
ingredients: 50g fresh yeast (or 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk, then stir in sugar, cardamom, and salt.
Add half the flour and mix, then work in the softened butter and remaining flour until you have a smooth dough. Knead for about 10 minutes.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Roll the dough out into a large rectangle on a floured surface, then spread with softened butter and sprinkle evenly with brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll the dough up tightly into a long log, then cut into 16-18 slices.
Place the buns cut-side up in paper cases or on a lined baking sheet, cover, and let rise for 45 minutes.
Brush the buns with beaten egg and sprinkle with pearl sugar.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 8-10 minutes until golden brown, then cool on a wire rack.

title: Prinsesstårta (Princess Cake)
ingredients: 400g green marzipan, rolled into a large thin sheet
instructions: Whisk the eggs and sugar together until pale, thick, and tripled in volume.
Sift together the flour, potato starch, and baking powder, then fold gently into the egg mixture.
Pour into a greased and lined round cake tin and bake at 175°C (350°F) for about 25 minutes. Cool completely, then slice horizontally into three layers.
Place the bottom sponge layer on a cake board and spread with raspberry jam, then top with a layer of vanilla pastry cream.
Add the second sponge layer and spread with a generous dome of whipped cream, mounding it higher in the center.
Top with the final sponge layer, pressing down gently to create the traditional dome shape.
Drape the rolled green marzipan sheet over the entire cake, smoothing it down the sides and trimming the excess.
Dust with powdered sugar and finish with a marzipan rose on top.

title: Kladdkaka (Sticky Chocolate Cake)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a springform pan, about 22-24cm in diameter.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, and vanilla sugar together until light and slightly foamy.
Sift in the flour, cocoa powder, and salt, and stir until just combined.
Fold in the melted butter until the batter is smooth and glossy.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 15-20 minutes, until the edges are set but the center is still soft and slightly wobbly.
Remove from the oven and let cool in the pan; the center will remain fudgy and dense as it cools.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve in wedges with lightly whipped cream.

title: Ostkaka (Swedish Warm Cheesecake)
ingredients: 2 tbsp rennet (junket) or rennet tablets dissolved in water
Fruit jam and whipped cream, for serving
instructions: Warm the milk to about 37°C (body temperature), then stir in the rennet and let it stand undisturbed until firmly set into curds, about 30-45 minutes.
Break up the set curds gently with a fork, then drain off some of the excess whey through a sieve, leaving the mixture moist but not swimming in liquid.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, and flour together, then fold in the curds, chopped almonds, almond extract, and cream.
Pour the mixture into a well-buttered baking dish.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 45-60 minutes, until the top is golden brown and the custard is just set with a slight wobble.
Serve warm or at room temperature with fruit jam and lightly whipped cream.

title: Wallenbergare
ingredients: 1 tbsp fresh dill or parsley, chopped, for serving
instructions: In a bowl, mix the ground veal with potato starch, salt, and white pepper.
Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then gradually work in the cream a little at a time until the mixture is smooth, light, and well combined.
Shape the mixture into 8 oval patties.
Coat each patty thoroughly in the dried breadcrumbs, pressing gently so the crumbs adhere.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium-low heat and fry the patties gently for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through, being careful not to burn the breadcrumbs.
Serve hot with creamy mashed potatoes, lingonberry jam, and a sprinkle of chopped dill or parsley.

title: Flygande Jacob
ingredients: 600g boneless chicken breast, sliced into strips
1-2 tsp sambal oelek or chili sauce, to taste
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Season the chicken strips with salt and pepper, then fry in butter or oil until browned on the outside, but not fully cooked through.
Fry the chopped bacon in a separate pan until crisp.
Place the browned chicken in a greased baking dish and scatter the bacon and sliced bananas evenly over the top.
Whisk together the cream, chili sauce, and sambal oelek, then pour evenly over the chicken, bacon, and bananas.
Sprinkle the peanuts over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is bubbling.
Serve hot with cooked rice.

title: Renskav (Sautéed Reindeer in Cream Sauce)
ingredients: 500g thinly sliced reindeer meat (or substitute thinly sliced beef if unavailable)
instructions: Melt half the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté the sliced onion until soft and lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
Increase the heat, add the remaining butter, and quickly sear the reindeer slices in batches so the pan stays hot, cooking just until browned but not overcooked.
Return the onions to the pan along with the crushed juniper berries.
Pour in the cream and soy sauce, stirring to combine, and let the sauce simmer for a few minutes until slightly thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot over mashed potatoes, with lingonberry jam and pickled cucumber on the side.

title: Dillkött (Veal in Dill Sauce)
ingredients: 800g veal shoulder or breast, cut into cubes
3 tbsp fresh dill, chopped, plus extra to garnish
instructions: Place the veal in a large pot, cover with the water, and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam that rises to the surface.
Add the onion, bay leaf, peppercorns, and salt, then reduce heat and simmer gently, covered, for about 1 hour until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat with a slotted spoon and strain the cooking liquid, reserving about 600ml of the stock.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for a minute, then gradually whisk in the reserved stock to form a smooth sauce.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes, then stir in the vinegar and sugar to balance the flavor with a gentle sweet-sour note.
Return the veal to the sauce and heat through, then stir in the chopped dill just before serving.
If desired, temper an egg yolk with a little hot sauce and stir it back in off the heat to enrich the sauce.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes, garnished with extra dill.

title: Kalvsylta (Veal in Aspic)
ingredients: 2 tsp powdered gelatin (if needed to strengthen the set)
Lingonberry jam and mustard, for serving
instructions: Place the veal and pork hock in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Add the onion, bay leaves, peppercorns, and salt, then reduce heat and simmer gently, covered, for 2-3 hours until the meat is very tender and falling off the bone.
Remove the meat and set aside to cool slightly, then strain and reserve the cooking broth.
Shred or finely chop the meat, discarding bones, skin, and fat, and season generously with white pepper and additional salt to taste.
Pack the meat tightly into a loaf pan or terrine mold.
Reduce the reserved broth over high heat until well concentrated, then dissolve the gelatin into it if the broth needs extra setting strength.
Pour the hot broth over the packed meat until just covered, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight until firmly set.
Unmold and slice thinly, serving cold with lingonberry jam and mustard.

title: Blodpudding (Swedish Blood Pudding)
ingredients: 150g dark rye flour or a mix of rye and wheat flour
Fried streaky pork or bacon, for serving
instructions: Strain the blood through a fine sieve into a large bowl to remove any clots, then whisk in the water.
Add the flour gradually, whisking constantly to avoid lumps, until you have a smooth, pourable batter.
Stir in the salt, allspice, cloves, dark syrup, and raisins.
Pour the mixture into greased loaf pans or traditional pudding molds, filling only about three-quarters full.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) in a water bath for about 1 hour, or steam the puddings, until firm and set throughout.
Let cool, then unmold and slice into thick pieces.
Fry the slices in butter until crisp and heated through.
Serve hot with fried pork or bacon and lingonberry jam.

title: Isterband (Swedish Cured Sausage)
ingredients: 200g barley groats or pearl barley, cooked
Lingonberry jam and pickled beets, for serving
instructions: Mix the ground pork with the cooked barley, mashed potatoes, salt, white pepper, and allspice until well combined.
Rinse the sausage casings and fit them onto a sausage funnel or piping bag.
Fill the casings with the meat mixture, twisting into links about 12-15cm long, and tie off the ends securely.

Traditionally, hang and lightly smoke or cold-cure the sausages for a day to develop their characteristic tangy flavor; alternatively, refrigerate the fresh sausages for a few hours to firm up before cooking.
Prick the sausages lightly and poach gently in barely simmering water for about 15 minutes until cooked through.
Fry the poached sausages in butter until golden and crisp on the outside.
Serve hot with boiled potatoes, lingonberry jam, and pickled beets.

title: Surströmmingsklämma
ingredients: 4 pieces tunnbröd (soft Swedish flatbread) or thin crispbread
150g creamy sour cream or crème fraîche
instructions: Open the can of surströmming outdoors or in a well-ventilated area, as it releases a very strong odor, then drain the fish and remove the fillets from the bones and skin.
Spread each piece of soft tunnbröd lightly with butter.
Layer sliced boiled potatoes over the bread, followed by a generous dollop of sour cream or crème fraîche.
Add a portion of the surströmming fillets on top.
Sprinkle with chopped red onion and chives.
Fold or roll the flatbread around the filling to enclose it, pressing gently to hold together.
Serve immediately while the bread is soft and pliable.

title: Smørrebrød med Marineret Sild (Rye Bread with Pickled Herring)
ingredients: 1 small red onion, thinly sliced into rings
instructions: Spread each slice of rye bread generously with softened butter, all the way to the edges
Lay a lettuce leaf on each slice to keep the bread crisp
Cut the pickled herring fillets into bite-sized pieces and arrange several pieces on top of each slice
Scatter red onion rings and capers over the herring
Top with slices of hard-boiled egg and a sprinkle of fresh dill
Serve open-faced immediately with lemon wedges, eaten with a knife and fork

title: Smørrebrød med Roastbeef og Remoulade (Roast Beef and Remoulade Sandwich)
ingredients: 300g cold rare roast beef, thinly sliced
instructions: Butter the rugbrød slices to the edges
Drape the thinly sliced roast beef in loose folds over each slice
Spoon remoulade over the beef
Top with crispy fried onions and a small mound of grated horseradish
Garnish with pickled cucumber slices and a sprig of parsley
Serve immediately as an open-faced sandwich

title: Smørrebrød med Leverpostej (Liver Pâté Sandwich)
ingredients: 300g warm homemade or store-bought leverpostej (liver pâté)
fresh cress or parsley for garnish
instructions: Butter the rugbrød slices to the edges
Spread a thick, even layer of warm leverpostej over each slice
Top with crisp bacon slices and sautéed mushrooms
Add a few slices of pickled beetroot alongside the topping
Garnish with cress or parsley and serve at once while the pâté is still warm

title: Frikadeller (Danish Pork Meatballs)
ingredients: 500g ground pork (or a mix of pork and veal)
instructions: In a bowl, mix the grated onion, egg, flour, salt, pepper, and allspice into the ground meat until well combined
Gradually beat in the milk a little at a time until the mixture becomes light and slightly sticky
Cover and let the mixture rest in the refrigerator for 20 minutes
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat
Using two spoons, shape the mixture into oval dumplings and lower them into the hot butter
Fry for about 5-6 minutes per side, until deeply golden brown and cooked through
Serve hot with boiled potatoes, brown gravy, and pickled red cabbage or cucumber salad

title: Flæskesteg (Danish Roast Pork with Crackling)
ingredients: 1.5kg pork loin roast with skin, scored in parallel lines
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F)
Make sure the rind is scored into narrow, even strips down to the fat; rub coarse salt deep into every cut
Tuck a small piece of bay leaf into every second or third cut in the rind
Place the roast rind-side up on a rack over a roasting pan and rub the oil over the rind
Roast for about 1.5 to 2 hours, until the internal temperature reaches 65-68°C and the rind has puffed into crisp crackling
If the crackling needs more crisping, increase the oven to 220°C for the final 10-15 minutes
Rest the roast for 10 minutes, then make gravy from the pan drippings whisked with flour and stock
Carve into slices along the scored lines and serve with the gravy, boiled or caramelized potatoes, and rødkål

title: Stegt Flæsk med Persillesovs (Fried Pork Belly with Parsley Sauce)
ingredients: 600g pork belly, sliced into 1cm thick strips
instructions: Season the pork belly slices with salt and pepper
Fry the slices in a dry, hot pan over medium heat for 8-10 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp, working in batches
Drain the fried pork on paper towels and keep warm
For the sauce, melt the butter in a saucepan and whisk in the flour to form a roux, cooking for 1 minute
Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer for 5-8 minutes, stirring often, until smooth and thickened
Stir the chopped parsley into the sauce just before serving and season with salt and pepper
Serve the crisp pork belly with boiled potatoes and the parsley sauce poured over the potatoes

title: Rødgrød med Fløde (Red Berry Compote with Cream)
ingredients: 3 tbsp cold water, to dissolve the starch
instructions: Combine the berries, water, and sugar in a saucepan and bring to a gentle boil
Simmer for about 5 minutes, then strain through a sieve, pressing to extract the juice, or leave some fruit pieces in if preferred
Return the juice to the pan and bring back to a light boil
Dissolve the potato starch in the cold water and whisk it into the simmering juice
Bring just back to a boil, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens slightly, then remove from the heat immediately
Pour into individual bowls and sprinkle the surface with a little sugar to prevent a skin from forming
Chill for at least 2 hours before serving with cold cream poured over and a scatter of chopped almonds

title: Æbleflæsk (Fried Pork Belly with Apples and Onions)
ingredients: 500g pork belly, sliced into thin strips
instructions: Fry the pork belly strips in a dry skillet over medium heat until crisp and golden, then remove and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pan
Add the sliced onion to the fat and sauté until soft and lightly caramelized
Add the apple slices and sugar and cook, stirring gently, until the apples are tender but still hold their shape
Season with thyme, salt, and pepper
Return the crisp pork belly to the pan and toss gently with the apples and onions to combine
Serve warm, spooned over slices of rugbrød

title: Gule Ærter (Danish Yellow Split Pea Soup)
ingredients: 400g dried yellow split peas, soaked overnight
500g salted or smoked pork (flæsk), in one piece
instructions: Drain the soaked split peas and place them in a large pot with the pork and enough water to cover generously
Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam, then reduce to a simmer and add the bay leaves and thyme
Simmer covered for about 1 to 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas have broken down into a thick soup
Add the carrots, leek, and onion and continue simmering for 20-25 minutes until the vegetables and pork are tender
About 15 minutes before serving, add the medisterpølse whole to gently poach it in the soup
Remove the pork and sausage, slice them, and season the soup with salt and pepper
Serve the soup in bowls with the sliced pork and sausage alongside, with mustard and rugbrød on the side

title: Hakkebøf (Danish Minced Beef Patties)
ingredients: 1 tsp soy sauce or dark gravy browning (optional)
instructions: Season the ground beef with salt and pepper and shape into four flat, round patties, pressing a shallow dimple into the center of each
Melt half the butter in a skillet and fry the onions over medium-low heat until soft and golden, about 15 minutes, then remove and set aside
Add the remaining butter to the pan and fry the patties over medium-high heat for about 4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked to preference
Remove the patties and keep warm
Whisk the flour into the fat remaining in the pan and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the beef stock to make a smooth gravy
Simmer the gravy for a few minutes until thickened, seasoning with salt, pepper, and a little soy sauce for color if desired
Serve the patties topped with the fried onions and gravy, alongside boiled potatoes

title: Medisterpølse (Danish Spiced Pork Sausage)
ingredients: 150g pork back fat, finely diced or ground
instructions: Mix the ground pork and back fat with the grated onion, salt, pepper, allspice, and cloves
Gradually work in the cold milk until the farce is smooth and well combined
Rinse the sausage casings and thread them onto a sausage funnel or piping bag fitted with a wide tip
Fill the casings evenly with the meat mixture, twisting into one long coil or into links, avoiding air pockets
Prick the sausage a few times with a needle, then poach gently in barely simmering water for about 20 minutes, or fry slowly in a pan until cooked through
Serve sliced or whole with boiled potatoes, stewed cabbage, and mustard

title: Leverpostej (Danish Liver Pâté)
ingredients: 250g pork back fat or lard, plus extra for topping
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a terrine or loaf dish
Grind or blend the liver, pork fat, anchovies, and onion together until very smooth, in batches in a food processor if needed
Whisk the flour into a little of the milk to form a smooth paste, then blend it into the liver mixture along with the remaining milk
Beat in the eggs, salt, pepper, and allspice until the mixture is completely smooth
Pour the mixture into the prepared dish and cover the top with a thin layer of extra pork fat
Place the dish in a larger roasting pan and add hot water halfway up the sides to create a water bath
Bake for about 1 to 1.5 hours, until set and golden on top, then cool completely before slicing
Serve cold or warm on rugbrød, or as part of a smørrebrød platter

title: Wienerbrød (Danish Pastry)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in the cold milk, then mix with the flour, sugar, salt, and egg to form a smooth dough; knead briefly and chill for 30 minutes
Roll the dough into a rectangle and place the cold butter block in the center; fold the dough over the butter to enclose it completely
Roll out the dough and fold it in thirds like a letter; wrap and chill for 20 minutes, then repeat this rolling and folding two more times, chilling between each turn
Mix the softened butter, sugar, and cardamom together to make the remonce filling
Roll the laminated dough out thin, cut into squares or strips, spread with the remonce, and shape into pinwheels, snails, or pretzel shapes
Arrange the pastries on baking trays, cover loosely, and let proof in a warm place for about 45 minutes until puffy
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 12-15 minutes until golden brown and flaky
Cool slightly and drizzle with a thin powdered sugar icing before serving

title: Kartoffelsalat (Danish Potato Salad)
ingredients: 2 tbsp sour cream or crème fraîche
instructions: Boil the potatoes whole in salted water until just tender, about 15-20 minutes, then drain and let cool slightly
Peel the potatoes while still warm if desired, then cut into bite-sized cubes or slices
Whisk together the mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, and vinegar in a large bowl
Gently fold the warm potatoes and chopped red onion into the dressing so the potatoes absorb the flavor
Season with salt and pepper to taste
Cover and chill for at least an hour, then stir in most of the chives, reserving some for garnish before serving

title: Rødkål (Sweet-Sour Braised Red Cabbage)
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot and sprinkle in the sugar, letting it caramelize slightly
Add the shredded red cabbage and stir to coat it in the caramelized butter
Pour in the vinegar and water, then add the grated apple and cloves
Cover and simmer gently over low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is very tender
Stir in the redcurrant jelly during the last 10 minutes of cooking and season with salt
Remove the whole cloves before serving warm alongside roast pork or duck

title: Boller i Karry (Meatballs in Curry Sauce)
ingredients: 1 small onion, grated, plus 1 onion sliced for the sauce
instructions: Mix the ground meat with the grated onion, egg, flour, milk, salt, and pepper to form a smooth meatball mixture
Shape the mixture into small meatballs and set aside
Melt the butter in a large saucepan and sauté the sliced onion and diced apple until softened
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant
Pour in the stock and bring to a gentle simmer, then carefully lower in the meatballs
Simmer the meatballs in the curry broth for about 10-12 minutes until cooked through
Stir in the cream and simmer a few minutes more to thicken slightly, seasoning to taste
Serve hot over cooked white rice

title: Æggekage (Danish Egg Dish with Bacon and Chives)
ingredients: rye bread and sliced tomatoes, for serving
instructions: Fry the bacon slices in a large ovenproof skillet until crisp, then set aside, leaving the fat in the pan
Whisk the eggs with the flour until smooth, then whisk in the milk and salt to make a thin batter
Melt the butter in the same skillet over low heat
Pour in the egg batter and cook gently over low heat, occasionally drawing the edges toward the center, until mostly set but still creamy on top
Arrange the fried bacon over the top of the egg mixture
Sprinkle generously with fresh chives and serve straight from the pan with rye bread and sliced tomatoes

title: Hindbærsnitter (Raspberry Jam Pastry Slices)
instructions: Rub the cold butter into the flour, sugar, and baking powder until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs
Add the egg and bring the dough together quickly without overworking it; divide in half, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes
Roll each half of the dough into a thin rectangle of the same size and place on baking sheets
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 10-12 minutes until just lightly golden, then cool completely
Spread the raspberry jam evenly over one baked rectangle and top with the second to form a sandwich
Whisk the powdered sugar with water to make a thick icing and spread it over the top layer
Scatter with colorful sprinkles before the icing sets, then cut into rectangular slices

title: Klejner (Fried Christmas Pastry Twists)
ingredients: neutral oil or lard, for deep-frying
instructions: Beat the eggs and sugar together until pale, then mix in the melted butter and cream
Sift in the flour, cardamom, and baking powder, and work into a smooth, firm dough; wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes
Roll the dough out thin on a floured surface and cut into diamond shapes about 8cm long
Cut a small slit in the center of each diamond and pull one pointed end through the slit to twist the klejne
Heat oil or lard to 175°C (350°F) in a deep pot
Fry the klejner in small batches for about 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown
Drain on paper towels and dust lightly with powdered sugar once cool

title: Risalamande (Danish Christmas Rice Pudding)
ingredients: 1 vanilla bean, split, or 1 tsp vanilla extract
100g blanched almonds, chopped, plus 1 whole almond
500g cherries or jarred sour cherries, for the sauce
3 tbsp sugar, for the cherry sauce
1 tbsp cornstarch, for the cherry sauce
instructions: Bring the milk to a boil with the vanilla bean, then stir in the rice, reduce to a low simmer, and cover
Cook the rice porridge gently for 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and tender, then stir in the sugar and let cool completely
Remove the vanilla bean, then fold the whipped cream and chopped almonds into the cooled rice porridge, along with the single whole almond
Chill the risalamande until ready to serve
For the cherry sauce, simmer the cherries with sugar and a splash of water until softened
Dissolve the cornstarch in a little cold water and stir into the simmering cherries until the sauce thickens slightly, then cool
Spoon the risalamande into bowls, top with warm cherry sauce, and serve; traditionally whoever finds the whole almond wins a small prize
